### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

all of the above

### Question

I have set up a newly installed neovim v0.13.0-dev-613+g1a7ab1ab47 using the MiniMax config starter. To register new languages with Treesitter I edited the `40_plugins.lua` file a shown:
```
  add({
    "https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter",
    "https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects",
  })

  -- Define languages which will have parsers installed and auto enabled
  -- After changing this, restart Neovim once to install necessary parsers. Wait
  -- for the installation to finish before opening a file for added language(s).
  local languages = {
    -- These are already pre-installed with Neovim. Used as an example.
    -- Add here more languages with which you want to use tree-sitter
    "lua",
    "vimdoc",
    "markdown",
    "bash",
    "bibtex",
    "css",
    "gitignore",
    "gpg",
    "html",
    "html_tags",
    "javascript",
    "latex",
    "regex",
    "ruby",
    "toml",
    "yaml",
    -- To see available languages:
    -- - Execute `:=require('nvim-treesitter').get_available()`
    -- - Visit 'SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.md' file at
    --   https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/blob/main
  }
  local isnt_installed = function(lang)
    return #vim.api.nvim_get_runtime_file("parser/" .. lang .. ".*", false) == 0
  end
  local to_install = vim.tbl_filter(isnt_installed, languages)
  if #to_install > 0 then
    require("nvim-treesitter").install(to_install)
  end

  -- Enable tree-sitter after opening a file for a target language
  local filetypes = {}
  for _, lang in ipairs(languages) do
    for _, ft in ipairs(vim.treesitter.language.get_filetypes(lang)) do
      table.insert(filetypes, ft)
    end
  end
  local ts_start = function(ev)
    vim.treesitter.start(ev.buf)
  end
  Config.new_autocmd("FileType", filetypes, ts_start, "Start tree-sitter")
end)

```
I ran  `:restart`  and `:TSUpdate` and confirmed that the listed parsers were downloaded to `~/.local/share/nvim/site/parser`. I also installed `tree-sitter-cli` and added the parser path to `~/.config//tree-sitter/config.json  parser-directories list.

However, Treesitter syntax highlighting only activates for the builtin filetypes: markdown, lua and vimdoc but not for any of the parsers I added like bash, latex or ruby. I have probably missed a step, but I can't see where. Can anyone help?

comment_data.body:
It seems to work for me at least for latex and ruby files. I had to make sure that the latex file is not just `.*.tex` as it is not recognized as LaTeX by default (but `plaintex` filetype instead).

> However, Treesitter syntax highlighting only activates for the builtin filetypes: markdown, lua and vimdoc but not for any of the parsers I added like bash, latex or ruby. I have probably missed a step, but I can't see where. Can anyone help?

Couple of clarifying questions:

- How do you determine that tree-sitter highlighting is not activated? The most convenient thing to do that is to put cursor on some highlighted text and execute `:Inspect`. If it mentions "Treesitter", then it is active in the current buffer.
- Did you run `:checkhealth vim.treesitter nvim-treesitter`?

---

Also, as this is a MiniMax question, it would have been better to ask directly in [`MiniMax` repo](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/discussions/categories/q-a). So I moved it.

reply_data.body:
> I did run `:checkhealth vim.treesitter nvim-treesitter` The first gave a big list of parsers marked `OK`. nvim-treesitter only reports installed languages as ...

This doesn't look right to me. The `vim.treesitter` checkhealth should also have a section "Treesitter queries" listing which queries it can recognize.

The output of `nvim-treesitter` checkhealth shows that there are no recognized queries for installed languages (like `ruby`). Here is the output of the fresh MiniMax config where only the above list of languages was added (after `:restart` and waiting for *all* languages to be installed):

```
Installed languages     H L F I J ~
- bash                  ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
- bibtex                ✓ . ✓ ✓ ✓
- css                   ✓ . ✓ ✓ ✓
- ecma
- gitignore             ✓ . . . ✓
- gpg                   ✓ . . . ✓
- html                  ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
- html_tags
- javascript            ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
- jsx
- latex                 ✓ . ✓ . ✓
- regex                 ✓ . . . .
- ruby                  ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
- toml                  ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
- yaml                  ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓
```

So I am afraid, there might be something going on either in other part of the config or system-wide. Couple more questions:
- Do you have this behavior in a fresh separate config or as a replacement for the old one? If the second one (and maybe even the first one), make sure that there is no 'lazy.nvim' installation affecting the installation (if you used one before).
- If the above does not help, then I'd ask to try to reproduce this in a fully separate config where the only change is the added new languages. Like `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-minimax` or another previously unused one, as described [here](https://nvim-mini.org/MiniMax/#setting-up). This will help to determine if the problem is on Neovim or overall system level.

reply_data.body: Thanks, I tried the install again as you suggested with `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-minimax` and just added the languages. This time everything worked well. Output of `:checkhealth vim.treesitter nvim-treesitter` is [here](https://gist.github.com/passmore/f0f6be73d7df7fb0ce05c8874b518b78). I've never installed `lazy.nvim` but have experimented with a variety of Neovim configs, most recently using `Lazy` and `Mason`, but wanting to simplify things as Treesitter and vim.pack have become built-in in recent releases. I think MiniMax is a great help with this, but I guess I didn't clean up well enough before moving it to `~/.config/nvim/`. Thanks again for your help.

reply_data.body:
> I've never installed `lazy.nvim` but have experimented with a variety of Neovim configs, most recently using `Lazy` and `Mason` ...

The LazyVim distro is built around 'lazy.nvim' plugin manager. So if it was used as the main config (in `~/.config/nvim`), then it indeed was installed somewhere. It probably interfered with 'runtimepath' somehow and didn't make installed queries visible for the Neovim process.

As a side note, `Mason` is not a Neovim config, but a 'mason-org/mason.nvim' plugin which [MiinMax can work with](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/349d1ce9bdce6358e115bf4fef44e7982ffd4b57/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L150-L161) (and I personally use it).
